forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 22%. AGI-26 Society conference (July 27-30 SF) speaker list published this week — focused on AGI research community, not lab declarations. No fresh credible lab AGI declaration; no movement near the 3-researcher threshold. Amodei (Davos 2026) continues to point to ~2027 as his modal AGI year; Hassabis still ~50% by 2030 — these are not 'achieved' declarations. Nvidia/Huang's earlier 'we've achieved AGI' framing (Fortune, March) was widely contested and does not meet resolution criteria. ~31 months remain to deadline. With OpenAI/Microsoft contract having explicitly displaced the 'AGI' term with capability gates, lab-side declaration incentive remains weak. No reason to move from 22%.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class — paradigm-defining tech claims with <3-year horizons resolve YES <20% historically. Researcher surveys cluster median AGI year 2040-2047.

factors_up.factor: Frontier capability gains continuing (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind)
Amodei publicly anchoring 2027 — raises lab-led declaration risk
Enterprise deployment compressing capability discovery loops

factors_down.factor: OpenAI/Microsoft replaced 'AGI' clause with capability gates
No researcher consensus near 3-attestation threshold
31 months short relative to typical paradigm declaration lag

key_uncertainties: Whether commercial pressure produces a self-declared 'AGI' before genuine consensus
How resolution adjudicates partial economically-valuable autonomy claims
Speed of self-improving R&D loop
update_triggers: Public AGI declaration by frontier lab
2+ leading researchers attesting jointly
ARC-AGI v3 or equivalent benchmark cleared at human-expert level

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 24%. McKinsey (~200 cuts targeting research/back-office) and Accenture (~11,000 restructuring roles) layoffs continue to flow through, but these are within previously priced trajectory and not yet attributable as ≥33% sector-wide loss. Industry coverage (Fast Company, CNBC) frames consulting as 'squarely within the zone' of AI disruption — junior leverage ratios shrinking — but client-facing senior roles still largely intact. 4.5 years remain. Threshold (≥33%) is demanding and requires 2+ credible analyses attributing change primarily to AI. No movement in attribution evidence base this week.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class — sector-wide ≥33% revenue/jobs decline within 5 years of disruptive technology emergence — ~15-25% historical base rate.

factors_up.factor: Confirmed McKinsey/Accenture/Deloitte cuts indicating early-stage compression
Generative AI absorbing analyst-tier synthesis work increasingly visible
Macro AI spending ($725B 2026) creating displacement pressure

factors_down.factor: ≥33% threshold demanding; current cuts are 1-5% of headcount
Consulting demand for AI integration advice partially offsets disruption
Attribution standard requires 2+ credible analyses naming AI as primary driver

key_uncertainties: Speed of AI absorbing senior-tier consulting work, not just analyst work
Whether AI implementation revenue offsets traditional advisory loss
How attribution evidence consolidates in 2027-2029
update_triggers: Big-3 firm announcing >15% headcount reduction with AI attribution
Sector revenue data showing >10% YoY decline
Major analyst report (Gartner/IDC) projecting >25% sector compression by 2028

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 2%. PollCheck 7-poll average (20 May) has Labour third at 18.1% behind Reform 27.9% and Con 18.3%. YouGov 4-5 May: Reform 25%, Lab 18%, Con 17%, Grn 15%, LD 14%. Labour's polling has been in 17-20% band since March; no recovery signal. Reform's sustained lead now ~12 months. ~3.5 years to deadline (Dec 2029) leaves time for swing, but margin of recovery (10+pp) and durability of Reform lead make 'Labour largest by seats' a low-probability outcome. UK FPTP can produce vote/seat asymmetries favouring incumbents, providing residual upside.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class — incumbent party trailing by 10pp at mid-term with 3-4 years remaining recovering to win seat plurality — ~15-25%. Labour's specific trough (third place) is rarer, ~5-10%.

factors_up.factor: FPTP can favour Labour with split right-wing vote
3.5 years for recovery; mid-term polling unreliable
Reform unproven on national campaign delivery

factors_down.factor: Labour third in polls, sustained 12+ months
Approval ratings approaching previous govt's nadir
Reform lead durable across pollsters

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform sustains organisational delivery to GE
Whether Labour leadership shifts before election
Whether right-wing vote splits favouring Labour by seats
update_triggers: Labour returning to first/second in 7-poll average
Reform losing 5+pp sustained over a month
Major realignment event (coalition talks, leadership change)

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 78%. ~9-year horizon gives ample time for either lab declaration or 3-researcher attestation as capability gains continue. Amodei modal 2027, Hassabis ~50% by 2030 — both well inside window. Researcher survey medians (2040s) suggest right tail of distribution, but probabilistic mass within 2030-2035 substantial. Lab competitive pressure to declare 'AGI' likely intensifies as capabilities cross undisputed thresholds (autonomous economically-valuable task chains). Continued enterprise scaling, agentic systems, and self-improving R&D loops all bias upward.

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 7%. AEI updates (May 1, 8, 15) consistent with established pattern — PRC pursuing pressure and grey-zone activity (research vessels in Bashi Channel, expanded PLAN deployments around Balikatan 2026 exercises) but not crossing into kinetic blockade or invasion. Trump-Xi summit 13-15 May focused on trade with no strategic departure. Taiwan's HIMARS deployment to Penghu/Dongyin signals deterrence holding. ~3.5 years remaining. Resolution requires blockade >72hrs OR assault on Taiwan proper confirmed by 2+ major outlets — high threshold. PRC capability-readiness commentary continues to point to 2027+ as operational window.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class — major-power kinetic action against contested territory within 5-year window historical base rate ~5-10%.

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Up 3pp to 6%. April 2026 CPI release (ONS, this week) printed 2.8% annual, down from 3.3% in March — a 50bp single-month drop, driven by housing/household services (electricity, gas). Core CPI fell from 3.1% to 2.5%; services CPI from 4.5% to 3.2%. This is a faster disinflation than priced in yesterday. With 8 monthly readings remaining (May-Dec 2026) and current trajectory, the gap to the 2.0% threshold is ~80bp. Bank of England guidance remains for 2026 inflation slightly above target; OBR March outlook had CPI 2.4% (2026 avg). One sub-2% monthly print before year-end requires continued disinflation pace or a base-effect/energy surprise — still unlikely but materially less so than the 3% prior. Modest upward revision.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class — CPI falling >80bp in 8 months from a stable disinflationary regime ~10-20%.

factors_up.factor: April print faster than expected — momentum may carry
Services CPI dropping sharply (4.5%→3.2%)
Housing/energy base effects could create one-month dip

factors_down.factor: OBR central forecast remains above 2% for 2026
Core CPI still 2.5% — sticky services component
Goods CPI rising (2.1%→2.4%) — offsetting upward pressure

key_uncertainties: Whether services disinflation continues or stalls at 3%
Energy price evolution into winter 2026
Wage growth and labour market softening pace
update_triggers: Any monthly CPI print <2.3%
Bank of England revising 2026 path below 2%
Wage growth falling below 3.5% sustained

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 98%. July 31 2026 release. Trailer broke all-time records (718.6M views in 24 hours; 1B views in 4 days — first movie trailer ever to hit 1B). This signals exceptional pre-release momentum. Reference points: No Way Home grossed $1.92B in 2021-22; Deadpool & Wolverine $1.34B in 2024. Brand New Day's trailer outperformance suggests opening weekend and run will track No Way Home or higher. The $1.5B threshold sits comfortably below No Way Home and the trailer signals indicate above-trend trajectory. Five months between release and resolution provides ample legs. Residual 2pp downside from execution risk, calendar congestion, or quality-driven dropoff.
forecasts.base_rate: MCU Spider-Man franchise crossing $1.5B threshold — 1 of 3 prior solo films (No Way Home only). With record-breaking marketing performance, base rate adjusts upward significantly.

Five-month window post-release for run to play out

factors_down.factor: Quality/reception execution risk

International market performance, especially China

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Down 1pp to 98%. Latest credible reporting: Anthropic at $30B ARR (April 2026, per company; OpenAI disputes, claims true comparable is ~$22B). OpenAI at $25B+ (March 2026, The Information). Headline sum: $30B + $25B = $55B; adjusted (OpenAI's net basis): ~$47B. To reach $70B by Q4 2026, need ~$15-23B incremental ARR — implying ~28-50% growth in 6-9 months. Anthropic's recent trajectory ($14B→$30B Jan-April) supports this; OpenAI's $21.4B→$25B+ in 3 months also supports. Combined growth trajectory comfortably clears $70B even under conservative accounting. Slight downward revision because the OpenAI/Anthropic accounting dispute introduces methodological risk that could lower headline sum.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class — frontier AI lab ARR growth rates 60-100% annual in 2025-2026 sustaining through one more year — high probability given confirmed trajectory.

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 37%. OBR March 2026 EFO continues to project GDP per person growth averaging 1.1% pa 2026-2030, with TFP at 1% and labour supply growth falling to 0.5% by 2030 (lower migration, ageing). Combined potential output growth converges around 1.3-1.5% range. IPPR / IFS commentary this week reiterates 'narrow paths' for productivity recovery. For 2030s arithmetic mean of 10 annual growth rates to clear 1.5%, the UK requires either sustained productivity surprise (TFP returning to 1%+) or labour-supply reversal. Both plausible — AI productivity gains the leading upside — but base rate not high. No fresh data to shift from 37%.
forecasts.base_rate: UK decade-average real GDP growth >1.5% in post-2010 era — 0 of 2 prior decades cleared. With productivity-recovery scenarios possible, mid-range probability.

factors_up.factor: AI-driven productivity gains could materialise in 2030s
Capital deepening from increased investment
Potential migration policy shift restoring labour supply

factors_down.factor: OBR central path falls below 1.5%
Ageing-driven labour supply decline structural
Two decades of <1.5% precedent

key_uncertainties: Whether AI productivity gains materialise economy-wide by 2030s
